1. Heard Sri Sanjeev Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Virendra Pal Singh,
learned A.G.A for the State respondents and Sri Arvind Kumar Dixit, learned counsel for the
informant.

2.  The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the F.I.R. dated 14.1.2023 registered as Case Crime No. 13 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station Awagarh District Etah.
Further prayer has been made not to arrest the petitioner in the aforesaid case.

sentences.text: The matter was referred to the Mediation Centre vide order dated 27.7.2023.
As per mediation report, the parties are not willing for the mediation, although petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 4 appeared on both the dates.
We, therefore, proceed to hear the matter on merits.
4. Submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioners are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is submitted that entire dues were paid by the petitioner and thereafter e-mail was sent to the ARTO, Firozabad by John Deere Finance company on 17.1.2021 for removing the discharge of hypothecation and thereafter, the tractor was sold and therefore, no offence is made out.
5.

This aspect is seriously being disputed by the learned counsel for the informant on the ground that annexure 2 to the petition indicates that e-mail was sent @gmail.com whereas the company never uses the @gmail.com for the purpose of sending e-mail and there is material change in the description of the vehicle in the alleged e-mail and therefore, a forgery in respect of e-mail has also been clearly committed and vehicle was sold by the petitioners fraudulently and in any case,
cognizable offence is made out on bare reading of the FIR.
6.

Learned AGA has also supported the arguments of learned counsel for the informant and submitted that during investigation this fact has also been verified and therefore, a cognizable offence is made out.
7. Perusal of the impugned first information report prima facie reveals commission of cognizable offence.

8. Therefore, in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 and M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.
Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918 and in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.3262/2021 (Leelavati Devi @ Leelawati & another vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh) decided on 07.10.2021, no case has been made out for interference with the impugned first information report.

sentences.text: 9. Therefore, the writ petition is dismissed leaving it open for the petitioner to apply before the competent court for anticipatory bail/bail as permissible under law and in accordance with law.

10. At this stage, Sri Sanjeev Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner, in categorical terms submits that the amount of Rs. 25,000/- to be paid to the respondent no. 4 has not been claimed by the respondent no. 4 during mediation proceedings.
He prays that since the mediation has failed between the parties, the amount of Rs. 25,000/- to be paid to the respondent no. 4 may be refunded to the petitioners.

11. In such view of the matter, in case the amount of Rs. 25,000/- has not been claimed by the respondent no. 4, the Mediation Centre shall refund the amount of Rs. 25,000/- (out of the total amount of Rs. 30,000/- deposited by the petitioner) to the petitioner in accordance with the procedure, provided there is no other legal impediment.
